content:
To optimise a Google Business Profile, get five things right, in this order: a business name that matches your real signage with no added keywords, the most specific primary category plus only the few secondary categories that describe what your business *is*, a complete list of services or products written in customers' words, current real photos, and a website link that lands on a page matching what the searcher wanted. Then keep it alive with accurate hours, steady reviews and occasional updates. Google says local results are based mainly on relevance, distance and prominence, and that there is no way to pay for a better local ranking. A digital marketing agency in Pune cannot change your distance from a searcher, but it can make your profile as relevant and as credible as your business really is. This guide shows how, field by field.

It is written for owners of local businesses in and around Pune (clinics, salons, restaurants, coaching institutes, contractors, retailers and professional firms) who already have a verified profile and want it to bring more calls, direction requests and website visits. If you have not verified yet, or are unsure whether to show your address, sort those out first, because verification and the address setting affect everything below.

## How Google decides which local businesses to show

Google's own help page on local ranking names three main factors:

- **Relevance:** how well a Business Profile matches what someone is searching for. Complete, detailed information helps Google understand your business.
- **Distance:** how far the business is from the searcher, or from the location named in the search.
- **Prominence:** how well known the business is. Google says it considers information from across the web, such as links and articles, and that review count and ratings play a part.

Two practical consequences follow. First, much of what decides your visibility is outside the profile itself: your website, your reviews, mentions of your business elsewhere. Second, the profile fields you control mostly affect relevance, so the aim is to describe your business completely and accurately, not to fill fields with keywords. Our broader guide to [local SEO and the Google map pack in Pune](/blog/local-seo-google-map-pack-pune-2026) covers the off-profile factors; this article focuses on the profile.

## The business name: match the signboard, nothing more

Google's guidelines say your business name should reflect the real-world name used consistently on your storefront, website and stationery. Adding marketing taglines, service descriptions, locations, phone numbers or other extra words is not permitted and can lead to suspension.

So "Sharma Dental Clinic" is right. "Sharma Dental Clinic - Best Dentist in Kothrud, Root Canal & Implants" is a policy violation, however common it is on Maps.

We are often asked whether keyword-stuffed names rank better. Sometimes they appear to, for a while. But they are reported by competitors, removed by Google's systems and are one of the most frequent triggers of suspension we see. Recovering a suspended profile takes weeks and costs far more than any short-term gain. If your registered name genuinely includes a descriptive word, for example a hospital called "Pune Eye Hospital", that is fine, because it is the real name.

## Categories: the most important choice on the profile

Google asks you to choose the fewest categories that describe your overall core business, and to pick the most specific one that fits. Categories should complete the sentence "This business **is** a…", not list services or amenities.

### Choosing the primary category

The primary category carries the most weight. Choose it based on how customers search for what you mainly do:

- A clinic that does mostly orthodontics: "Orthodontist" rather than "Dentist", if orthodontics is the core of the practice.
- A firm that designs and executes home interiors: "Interior designer".
- A restaurant: the most specific cuisine category that is accurate, rather than just "Restaurant".

Look at the top three map results for your main search in your area. Their primary categories are a useful clue, though you should never copy a category that is not accurate for you. You can find the primary category of competitors by looking at the label under their name on Google Maps.

### Secondary categories

Add secondary categories only if they describe a genuinely separate thing your business is. A dental clinic that also runs a separate, staffed cosmetic dentistry practice might add it; a salon that sells a few hair products should not add "Beauty supply store". Too many loosely related categories can blur what Google thinks you are.

### Review categories when your business changes

If you add a new line of business, revisit categories. If your category list includes things you no longer do, remove them, because customers who find you for those terms will be disappointed and may leave negative reviews.

## Services and products: describe what you actually sell

Once the category is right, the services and products sections are where you add detail. Google lets you choose from suggested services tailored to your category and add custom services, with descriptions and, optionally, prices. Custom services that contain prices or phone numbers in the name, gibberish or personal information are rejected automatically.

### Writing services that help

- **Use customers' words.** "Kitchen modular interiors" rather than "Culinary space solutions". Check the queries in your profile's performance report and in Search Console for the words people actually use.
- **One service per line.** List "Root canal treatment", "Dental implants", "Teeth cleaning" separately rather than one entry called "All dental treatments".
- **Add a short, factual description** for each important service: what it includes, who it suits, how long it takes. Keep it plain. Descriptions that are only lists of keywords help nobody.
- **Add prices only if they are stable and honest.** A "from" price is fine if it is genuinely available. If your prices vary widely by job, leave the price out rather than showing a misleading low number.

### Products

The products section suits retailers, restaurants with set menus and businesses selling packaged services. Each product can have a photo, description, price and link. Regulated products such as alcohol, tobacco, gambling, financial services and certain medicines are not allowed in product listings. Keep products current; an out-of-stock or discontinued item shown on your profile creates unhappy calls.

## The description and the "from the business" section

The business description is limited to a few hundred characters and Google prohibits links, promotions and prices in it. Use it to say plainly what you do, for whom, where and what makes you different:

> Family dental clinic in Kothrud, Pune, open since 2012. We treat adults and children, with a dedicated orthodontics practice and same-week appointments for root canal treatment. Wheelchair-accessible ground-floor clinic with parking.

That example is illustrative, not a real clinic. Note what it does: names the area naturally once, describes services in plain words, and adds concrete details customers care about. It does not repeat "best dentist in Pune" five times.

## Photos and video: real, recent and specific

Google's guidelines call for photos that are in focus, well lit, without significant alterations or excessive filters, and that represent reality. Files should be JPG or PNG, between 10 KB and 5 MB, with 720 by 720 pixels recommended and 250 by 250 pixels as the minimum.

### What to upload

- **Exterior:** the building and entrance as a customer would see them, from the road and from close up, including the signboard. This helps people find you, especially in buildings with several businesses.
- **Interior:** reception, waiting area, work area, the space as it looks on a normal day.
- **Team:** people at work, with their permission.
- **Work:** finished projects, dishes, products, before-and-after results where that is appropriate and allowed in your profession.
- **Short videos:** a 20 to 30 second walk from the gate to the reception, or a quick look at a finished project.

### What to avoid

- Stock photos and images taken from other websites.
- Heavy filters, text-heavy promotional graphics and collages.
- Photos that show customers or patients without their consent. For health-related businesses, check your professional body's rules on before-and-after images and advertising.

Customers also upload photos to your profile. You cannot delete them, but you can report ones that are inappropriate or not of your business. Uploading good photos of your own regularly gives searchers a better first impression than a handful of dark customer snaps.

How often? There is no rule that you must upload weekly. A practical rhythm is to add new photos when something genuinely changes, such as a renovated space, a new team member, a seasonal menu or a new project, and to check the profile monthly.

## Hours, attributes and contact options

### Hours

Incorrect hours are among the most damaging errors on a profile: a customer drives across the city to a closed shutter and leaves a one-star review. Keep regular hours current and set **special hours** for festivals and holidays, such as Diwali, Ganesh Chaturthi and Gudi Padwa, well in advance. If you take appointments only, say so in the description and on your website.

### Attributes

Attributes describe facts such as wheelchair accessibility, parking, payment options, online appointments and whether the business is women-led. Fill in every attribute that is true. They help the searcher decide and can match specific searches.

### Phone, messaging and booking links

- Use a phone number that connects directly to the business location and is answered during business hours. Google does not accept premium-rate numbers.
- If you use call tracking, follow Google's guidance: put the tracking number as the primary number and your main business number as an additional number, so your listing stays consistent.
- If you accept bookings online, add an appointment link that goes straight to the booking page, not your homepage.

## The website link: where most profiles lose the customer

Many profiles send every click to the homepage. For a business with one main service, that may be fine. For businesses with several services or locations, it often is not.

- **Single location:** link to the homepage only if the homepage clearly states your services, area, contact details and a primary call to action on the first screen. Otherwise link to the most relevant page.
- **Several locations:** each location's profile should link to that location's own page on your website, with its address, hours, map, photos and local contact number. Build these as genuinely useful pages, not thin copies with the area name swapped.
- **Add UTM parameters** to the website link (for example `?utm_source=google&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=gbp`) so visits from your profile show separately in Google Analytics, instead of mixing with other organic search traffic.

### Make the website agree with the profile

Your name, address and phone number should be the same on the profile, on your website's contact page and footer, and in the structured data on your site. Your website's services pages should cover the services listed on the profile. Consistency helps Google trust both, and it helps customers who move between them. We cover the technical side, including LocalBusiness structured data and opening hours markup, in our guide to [LocalBusiness schema, NAP and opening hours](/blog/web-development-company-pune-localbusiness-schema-nap-opening-hours-2026).

## Reviews: the part of prominence you can influence

Google says that more reviews and positive ratings can help your local ranking, and recommends replying to reviews. The legitimate way to get more reviews is to ask every genuinely satisfied customer, at the right moment, with a direct link, and to reply to every review, positive or negative, politely and specifically.

Do not buy reviews, offer discounts in exchange for reviews or ask staff and family to post them. These breach Google's policies on fake engagement and can get reviews removed or the profile restricted. Our separate guide covers [getting more Google reviews legitimately](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-google-business-profile-reviews-2026) in detail, including when and how to ask.

## Updates, offers and events: useful, not magic

Google lets you add posts to your profile in three types: updates, offers and events. Offers and events need a title and start and end dates. Google archives posts older than six months unless they have a date range, and posts that include a phone number in the description may be rejected.

Posts are worth doing when you have something real to say: a seasonal menu, a free health camp, a new service, a festival offer, holiday timings. They give returning searchers a reason to click. We have not seen good evidence that posting on a fixed schedule improves ranking on its own, so if you are short of time, prioritise accurate information, photos and reviews over weekly posts.

## Questions and answers, and messages

Anyone can ask a question on your profile, and anyone can answer it. Check this section regularly. If people ask the same questions often, such as "Do you have parking?" or "Do you take insurance?", answer them clearly and add the answer to the description, the attributes and your website's FAQ.

If you enable chat or messaging features where available, only do so if someone will reply within working hours. An unanswered message is worse than no messaging option.

## Measuring what the profile does

The performance view in your Business Profile shows searches, views, calls, direction requests, website clicks and bookings, along with some of the search terms that triggered your profile. Look at it monthly and compare with the same month last year to account for seasonality.

Useful questions to ask:

- Are the search terms what you expected? If people find you mainly by your brand name, your profile is not yet showing for discovery searches like "physiotherapist near me".
- Which actions are growing: calls, directions or website clicks? This tells you where to focus.
- Do website visits tagged with your UTM link lead to enquiries? Track form submissions, calls and WhatsApp clicks as key events in Google Analytics so you can see what the profile actually brings.

Remember that local results vary by where the searcher is standing. Checking rankings from your own office tells you little. Grid-based rank tracking tools can show how visibility changes across different parts of the city, though you should treat their figures as indicative.

## A monthly checklist

Use this to keep the profile healthy in under an hour a month:

- [ ] Hours and special hours correct for the coming month
- [ ] At least a few new, real photos if anything has changed
- [ ] Every new review replied to
- [ ] New questions answered
- [ ] Services and products still accurate, prices still valid
- [ ] Website link and appointment link working
- [ ] Any suggested edits from Google or users reviewed and accepted or rejected
- [ ] Performance compared with last month and the same month last year

## What it costs to have this done

Basic optimisation of an existing, verified profile, covering categories, services, description, attributes, photos guidance, link tagging and a review request process, is typically a few days of work. Ongoing management, including review replies, monthly updates and reporting, is usually part of a local SEO retainer. Pricing varies widely by the number of locations and how much content and photography is involved; ask any agency for a written list of exactly what they will do each month. Be wary of anyone who guarantees a top-three map ranking, because Google itself says ranking cannot be bought, and distance from the searcher is outside anyone's control.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I optimise my Google Business Profile?

Use your real business name with no added keywords, choose the most specific primary category and only relevant secondary ones, list each service or product in customers' words, upload real recent photos, keep hours and special hours accurate, link to the most relevant page of your website, and ask satisfied customers for reviews and reply to them.

### Does adding keywords to my business name help ranking?

It may appear to help briefly, but it breaks Google's guidelines, which require the name to match your real-world signage. Profiles with stuffed names are often edited or suspended after reports from competitors or Google's systems. Use services, the description and your website to describe what you do.

### How many categories should I choose on Google Business Profile?

As few as describe your core business. Choose the most specific accurate primary category, then add secondary categories only for things your business genuinely is, not for every service you offer. Services belong in the services section.

### Do Google Business Profile posts improve local ranking?

There is no clear evidence that regular posting by itself improves ranking. Posts are useful for sharing real news, offers, events and holiday timings with people who see your profile. Prioritise accurate information, categories, photos and reviews first.

### Why is my business not showing in Google Maps results?

Common reasons are distance from the searcher, a primary category that does not match the search, an incomplete or unverified profile, few reviews, a suspended profile, or a website that does not support the profile. Searching from a different part of the city will also change results, so check visibility across several locations.
